2607.28478.title: Would You Walk to the Car Wash? Revealing the Salience Bias of Large Language Models in Commonsense Reasoning
2607.28478.paper_summary: As large language models (LLMs) continue to advance in complex reasoning tasks, they have learned to heavily prioritize explicit conditions provided in the input. However, in everyday commonsense reasoning, this mechanism exposes a critical vulnerability which we term Salience Bias: models become easily hijacked by useless explicit distractors (e.g., numerical values), leading them to ignore the implicit physical or commonsense prerequisites of a task. A critical open question is whether this failure reflects a genuine gap in commonsense knowledge or merely its suppression under misleading task framing. To investigate this, we construct the SaliTrap Benchmark, a high-quality dataset across four trap dimensions. Evaluating 12 state-of-the-art LLMs, we find that all mainstream models suffer significantly from salience bias, with severity scaling with distractor density and detecting the trap often decoupled from actually avoiding it. Crucially, by re-eliciting the same models with the task framing stripped away, we show that this is overwhelmingly a failure of \textbf{knowledge suppression rather than knowledge absence}: a context-free knowledge probe alone recovers over 90\% of sycophantic-compliance failures, revealing that the requisite commonsense is intrinsically present but actively crowded out by salient distractors that lure the model into over-compliant, unnecessary computation. Building on this diagnosis, we further show that lightweight, inference-time prompting alone substantially closes the gap without any retraining. Our findings relocate the bottleneck of commonsense reasoning failures from model competence to elicitation, and we release SaliTrap as a testbed for this blind spot. The codes are available at https://github.com/Wuzheng02/SaliTrap.
2607.28478.paper_summary_zh: 隨著大型語言模型（LLMs）在複雜推理任務中的持續進步，它們已經學會在輸入中高度優先考慮明確條件。<lb/>然而，在日常的常識推理中，這一機制暴露出一個關鍵的脆弱性，我們稱之為顯著性偏差：模型容易被無用的明確干擾項（例如，數值）劫持，導致它們忽視任務的隱含物理或常識前提。<lb/>一個關鍵的未解問題是，這一失敗是否反映了常識知識的真正缺口，還是僅僅是其在誤導性任務框架下的抑制。<lb/>為了調查這一點，我們構建了 SaliTrap 基準測試，一個涵蓋四個陷阱維度的高質量數據集。<lb/>在評估 12 個最先進的 LLM 時，我們發現所有主流模型都顯著受到顯著性偏差的影響，且其嚴重程度隨著干擾項的密度而增加，檢測陷阱與實際避免陷阱之間往往是脫鉤的。<lb/>至關重要的是，通過去除任務框架重新引導相同的模型，我們顯示這主要是知識抑制的失敗，而非知識缺失：一個無上下文的知識探測器單獨恢復了超過 90\% 的諂媚遵從失敗，顯示所需的常識本質上是存在的，但被顯著的干擾項主動擠出，這些干擾項引誘模型進入過度遵從和不必要的計算。<lb/>基於這一診斷，我們進一步顯示，輕量級的推理時提示單獨顯著縮小了差距，而無需任何再訓練。<lb/>我們的發現將常識推理失敗的瓶頸從模型能力轉移到了引導，我們將 SaliTrap 發佈為這一盲點的測試平台。<lb/>代碼可在 https://github.com/Wuzheng02/SaliTrap 獲得。
